subject_line: Your ketone number might be lying to you
opening: Happy Sunday, friend. This week the community had a lot to say about blood meters, nosy strangers, and whether your carnivore plate is anyone else's business. We pulled the best of it together so you don't miss a thing.

hero.title: Why Everyone's Obsessing Over Their Ketone Numbers
hero.teaser: Blood meters are everywhere right now, and people are posting their ketone readings like a badge of honor. But here's the thing nobody's saying out loud: a high number doesn't automatically mean you're doing better. Chloe digs into what the community is actually seeing, and why chasing a specific number might be sending people in the wrong direction. The answer will probably change how you look at your next reading.
hero.cta: Read before your next finger prick

supporting.title: Keto Without Exercise: What Actually Happens
supporting.teaser: Marcus gives you the honest answer on what skipping the gym really costs you, and it's not what most people expect.

supporting.title: When Strangers Comment on Your Plate
supporting.teaser: Community members shared exactly what they say back, and a few of those responses are genuinely brilliant.

supporting.title: OMAD and Marathon Training: Can You Do Both?
supporting.teaser: Marcus found a way to structure it, but there's one condition that most OMAD fans won't like hearing.

try_this_week: Track how you feel, not just what your meter says. This week, log one note next to each ketone reading: energy level, sleep quality, or mood. By Friday, you'll have actual data on whether your number matches your performance, and that context is worth more than any single reading on its own.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something a lot of you have been asking about: what happens to your hormones after six months on carnivore, and whether the answer should make you nervous or excited.
